$ relay serve --help
Usage: relay serve [options]

Print the options of the server.

Options:
      --addr string              Address to listen on.      default ":8080", env RELAY_SERVE_ADDR, key serve.addr
      --allow string,...         Origins that may connect.  env RELAY_SERVE_ALLOW, key serve.allow
      --route string=string,...  Upstream of each path.     env RELAY_SERVE_ROUTE, key serve.route
      --tls-cert string          Certificate file.          env RELAY_SERVE_TLS_CERT, key serve.tls.cert
      --url string               URL of the database.       default "postgres://localhost/relay", env RELAY_SERVE_URL, key database.url

Global options:
  -c, --config file  Config file in JSON or INI.                                             default "relay.json", env RELAY_CONFIG
      --flag-debug   Print the value and the source of each option before the command runs.  env RELAY_FLAG_DEBUG
  -h, --help         Show the help.
[exit 0]

$ cat relay.json
{
  "database": {"url": "postgres://db.internal/relay"},
  "serve": {
    "addr": ":9000",
    "allow": ["https://app.example.com", "https://admin.example.com"],
    "route": {"/api": "http://api:8080", "/static": "http://cdn:8080"},
    "tls": {"cert": "relay.pem"}
  },
  "migrate": {"steps": 3}
}
$ relay serve
listen on :9000 with "relay.pem"
database postgres://db.internal/relay
allow ["https://app.example.com" "https://admin.example.com"]
route /api to http://api:8080
route /static to http://cdn:8080
[exit 0]

$ cat relay.json
{
  "database": {"url": "postgres://db.internal/relay"},
  "serve": {
    "addr": ":9000",
    "allow": ["https://app.example.com", "https://admin.example.com"],
    "route": {"/api": "http://api:8080", "/static": "http://cdn:8080"},
    "tls": {"cert": "relay.pem"}
  },
  "migrate": {"steps": 3}
}
$ relay migrate
migrate postgres://db.internal/relay, steps 3
[exit 0]

$ cat relay.ini
; Copyright Stealth Scale B.V. 2026
; SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

; This file contains the options of relay.json in INI. A section contains the keys of a command, a
; group or a map. A value is text, so commas separate the values of a list.

[database]
url = postgres://db.internal/relay

[serve]
addr = :9001
allow = https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com

[serve.route]
/api = http://api:8080

[serve.tls]
cert = "relay ini.pem"

[migrate]
steps = 2
$ relay -c relay.ini serve
listen on :9001 with "relay ini.pem"
database postgres://db.internal/relay
allow ["https://app.example.com" "https://admin.example.com"]
route /api to http://api:8080
[exit 0]

$ cat relay.conf
; Copyright Stealth Scale B.V. 2026
; SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

; This file is in INI. app registers INI for the extension .conf.

[serve]
addr = :9002
$ relay -c relay.conf serve
listen on :9002 with ""
database postgres://localhost/relay
allow []
[exit 0]

$ cat relay.ini
; Copyright Stealth Scale B.V. 2026
; SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

; This file contains the options of relay.json in INI. A section contains the keys of a command, a
; group or a map. A value is text, so commas separate the values of a list.

[database]
url = postgres://db.internal/relay

[serve]
addr = :9001
allow = https://app.example.com,https://admin.example.com

[serve.route]
/api = http://api:8080

[serve.tls]
cert = "relay ini.pem"

[migrate]
steps = 2
$ RELAY_CONFIG=relay.ini relay migrate --steps 1
migrate postgres://db.internal/relay, steps 1
[exit 0]

$ cat typo.json
{
  "serve": {"adr": ":9000"}
}
$ relay -c typo.json serve
relay: serve: unknown key serve.adr in typo.json (did you mean serve.addr?)
[exit 2]

$ cat relay.json
{
  "database": {"url": "postgres://db.internal/relay"},
  "serve": {
    "addr": ":9000",
    "allow": ["https://app.example.com", "https://admin.example.com"],
    "route": {"/api": "http://api:8080", "/static": "http://cdn:8080"},
    "tls": {"cert": "relay.pem"}
  },
  "migrate": {"steps": 3}
}
$ relay serve >/dev/full
relay: main: write the options of the server: clitest: no space left on device
[exit 1]
